subject: Re: Renewal proposal — capacity ramp & transitional price hold
messages:
From: Amelia Chen <amelia.chen@sparkbridge.com>
To: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@sparkbridge.com
Date: 2027-10-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — upcoming Oct 31 renewal / capacity plan

Hi Rohan,

We’re starting renewal planning for SparkBridge (renewal date: 2027-10-31) and I wanted to get ahead of capacity planning. Our usage has grown ~2.6x this quarter due to the new recommender line. Procurement asked me to request a short-term price hold for the first quarter of the new term while we ramp (our CFO needs predictable unit cost for budgeting).

High level ask from our side: can Redwood lock current per-token pricing for Q4 (three months) while we increase committed capacity by +40% across embeddings and generation? We’re open to a true-up + phased commit (monthly cadence) and are also interested in a one-time onboarding credit to offset migration costs (data-transfer, eval runs).

Can you share:
- A short pricing proposal outlining: transitional price hold, commit uplift options, and any onboarding credit you can offer
- Target timelines for contract amendment and SOW update

I’ve attached the internal forecast and the current SOW for reference (attached: SparkBridge_SOW_v3.pdf).

Thanks,
Amelia
Amelia Chen
Head of Platform Engineering | SparkBridge

From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwoodinference.com>

Date: 2027-10-03T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — upcoming Oct 31 renewal / capacity plan

Hi Amelia — thanks for the context and the forecast. Looping in Kimberly (Finance) to validate a short-term price hold and Grace (CS) for the onboarding support plan.

Quick summary of what we can do and questions:

Proposal (initial):
- Transitional price hold: maintain current per-token rates for an initial 90-day period after the new term start (2027-11-01 - 2028-01-30).
- Commit uplift: staggered commit increase of +40% (month 1: +20% commit, month 2: +30%, month 3+: +40%) with a quarterly true-up.
- Onboarding credit: one-time credit equal to 10% of the first-quarter committed spend to cover migration/eval costs (applied as a billing credit).
- Burst/headroom: soft burst capacity available (up to 1.2x committed) with overage charge at published on-demand rates.

Questions for SparkBridge:
- Do you need a hard per-token price cap (no overage above the held price) or a billing credit to offset overages during ramp?
- Are there internal vendor approvals we should coordinate (PO timing / signatory)?

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly to confirm budget & accounting treatment for the credit and temporary price hold.
2) If approved, we’ll generate an amendment + updated SOW and a pricing workbook for sign-off (target: draft in 48 business hours).
3) Grace to schedule an onboarding kick-off and share a runbook for eval runs to minimize additional spend.

Attaching a draft pricing workbook (pricing_workbook_v2) — I’ll upload the official version to Drive once finance confirms.

Rohan

Thanks Rohan — that framework is helpful. Procurement has two follow-ups:

1) They prefer a hard price cap on per-token rates for the initial 90 days rather than credits applied after the fact — their treasury team wants immediate budget certainty.
2) They asked if the onboarding credit can be structured as a refundable usage credit (applied up-front as a credit balance) so it clearly offsets invoices.

Operational notes: our PO cycle is the week of Oct 18 and legal will need a redline window of at least one week. We aim to sign the amendment by Oct 25 to give engineering time to schedule the migration run.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can:
- Put a hard per-token price cap for the first 90 days;
- Issue the onboarding credit as an upfront billing credit applied to the account rather than a retroactive rebate;
- Deliver a draft amendment and SOW by Oct 6?

If those are possible we’ll aim to move fast on the PO.

--
Amelia
From: Rohan Mehta <rohan.mehta@redwoodinference.com>
To: Amelia Chen <amelia.chen@sparkbridge.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, legal-ops@redwoodinference.com
Date: 2027-10-05T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal proposal — capacity ramp & transitional price hold

Amelia — good news: Kimberly confirmed we can do both items with a small compliance caveat. Summary of the finalized approach: 

1) Price cap: Redwood will apply a hard per-token price cap for the first 90 days of the new term (documented in the amendment). Any usage above committed/burst will bill at the capped rate.
2) Onboarding credit: we will issue the onboarding credit as an upfront account credit (refundable balance) equal to 10% of first-quarter committed spend — applied immediately upon amendment execution.
3) Commit schedule: we’ll formalize the staggered commit (20%/30%/40%) in the pricing workbook and include a quarterly true-up clause; overages above 1.2x burst will invoice at on-demand rates.
4) Timeline: legal-ops will produce a draft amendment + SOW by 2027-10-06 end of day; target signature is 2027-10-25 to meet your internal PO cadence.

Action items:
- Kimberly: please confirm the exact credit accounting code and whether finance needs a vendor memo for SparkBridge.
- Grace: schedule a migration readiness call for Oct 11 and share the eval runbook (include recommended prompt sets and token budgets).
- Amelia / SparkBridge: confirm PO week (you noted Oct 18) and notify if legal requires any non-standard terms early.

Attachments: pricing_workbook_v2.xlsx (draft) — I’ll post the Drive link to the HubSpot deal.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this across the line.

Rohan Mehta
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
